messages:
John Carver (Customer): Hey team — since we switched the customer-managed gateway in our VPC (k8s/nginx ingress -> customer gateway pods) we're seeing intermittent 429s and big tail latency on /v1/generate. Pattern: happens during short bursts (a few hundred RPS for 20-40s). Response headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset with small window. Not seeing quota in our Redwood dashboard drop. Can we escalate? We need a repro path and a config tweak that doesn't require a full redeploy.

Priya Patel (Support): Thanks @John — we can help triage. Quick questions: did you switch to our customer-managed gateway recently and was any ratelimiting config changed on your side? Can you paste the gateway deployment args and the ingress annotations? Also send `kubectl get pods -n gateway -o wide` and `kubectl top pods -n gateway` if possible.

John Carver (Customer): We flipped to the customer-managed package yesterday. We didn't intentionally change rate limit annotations, only moved the gateway to the customer VPC and updated env vars for KMS. We do use nginx-ingress controller (community) in front of the gateway pods. Attach logs snippet below (sanitized):

```
[2026-03-14T14:12:01Z] INFO request_id=abc123 endpoint=/v1/generate status=429 reason=rate_limited remote_ip=10.0.2.45
[2026-03-14T14:12:01Z] DEBUG headers: X-RateLimit-Limit: 1000 X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 X-RateLimit-Reset: 14
[2026-03-14T14:12:02Z] WARN kvcache: miss for prefix abc123
[2026-03-14T14:12:05Z] INFO request_id=abc124 endpoint=/v1/embeddings status=200 latency_ms=360
```

We can repro with `hey -z 30s -c 200 -q 10 -m POST https://gw.example.com/v1/generate` — that seems to push the cluster into 429s.

Miguel Ramos (SRE): Thanks for the details. Two likely culprits: 1) ingress controller or k8s service/load-balancer fronting the gateway is enforcing connection/RPS limits (NGINX has default conn limits), 2) the gateway's local token-bucket limiter is configured conservatively after the VPC networking change (sudden NAT/concurrency differences expose burst behavior).

Immediate data collection steps (please run and paste outputs):
```
kubectl get pods -n gateway -o wide
kubectl describe deployment gateway -n gateway
kubectl logs -l app=customer-gateway -c gateway -n gateway --since=1h | grep -i rate_limited -n | tail -50
kubectl get hpa -n gateway
kubectl top pods -n gateway
kubectl get configmap nginx-ingress-controller -n ingress -o yaml
```

Also on the client side run a targeted curl to capture response headers: ``curl -i -X POST https://gw.example.com/v1/generate -d @payload.json -H 'Content-Type: application/json'`` and paste the X-RateLimit-* headers if present.

Lee Tan (Infra): A few notes on common gotchas we've seen with customer-managed gateways: the nginx ingress defaults can drop connections during bursts if `limit-connections` or `limit-rps` annotations exist on the Ingress or if the controller's `worker-shutdown-timeout`/`worker-processes` are too low. Also cloud NATs can fragment source IPs which affects per-IP ratelimiting.

Suggested quick mitigations (no code deploy):
- If you have control over the nginx ingress controller, temporarily scale ingress replicas up by 2x and bump worker-processes.
- Disable ingress-level RPS limits if set (annotation removal + reload)
- Add a short client-side jitter/retry (exponential backoff) to smooth bursts while we debug

Priya Patel (Support): If you prefer a config change, here are two options — one for nginx ingress annotations and one for the gateway's local limiter flags. Try the nginx change first because it doesn't require changing gateway binary args.

NGINX ingress annotations (example):
```
metadata:
  annotations:
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "0"   # disable controller RPS limit
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections: "0"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size: "100m"
    nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size: "8k"
```
Notes: set to 0 to disable controller-enforced RPS/connection caps temporarily. After disabling, do gradual rollback if you need protection against abusive clients.

Gateway (customer-gateway) token-bucket flags (requires restart):
```
--ratelimit-backend=local
--ratelimit-bucket-size=500   # allow larger bursts
--ratelimit-refill-interval=100ms
--ratelimit-refill-tokens=50
--max-concurrent-requests=2000
```
These flags are internal to the gateway binary (example names — your deployment may use env vars RWL_*). Increasing bucket-size and refill tokens increases tolerated bursts but will increase short-lived cost because more tokens are used per second.

Miguel Ramos (SRE): If you're using Envoy or the Redwood gateway with Envoy fronting, we also recommend offloading global counts to a Redis-backed rate-limit service rather than purely local token buckets. Example Envoy ext-auth/rate-limit snippet (very condensed):
```
rate_limits:
  - actions:
      - request_headers:
          header_name: ":path"
          descriptor_key: "/v1/generate"
```
And the rate limit service config (RLS) in front of Redis to keep counters consistent across pods. This prevents single-pod burst exhaustions.

John Carver (Customer): We're on the community nginx ingress + Service -> gateway ClusterIP -> gateway pods. We do not have an external Redis RLS. We're hesitant to restart gateway during business hours, but can patch ingress annotations. Trying that now and will scale ingress.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: patching ingress annotations for ingress-name gateway-ingress in namespace ingress (user: john.c) — rollout in progress :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Priya Patel (Support): While that's rolling, please capture a few more runtime metrics (helpful for SRE):
- gateway pod CPU/heap traces: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -n gateway -- curl localhost:9000/metrics | grep request_duration`
- ingress controller metrics for connections/requests: typically at `/metrics` port 10254 or 9113 depending on controller

John Carver (Customer): Patch applied. We removed limit-rps/limit-connections annotations and scaled ingress from 2 -> 5 replicas. Running the same `hey` repro now. Preliminary: burst lasted longer before 429s, tail latency improved from 900ms p95 down to ~420ms p95. Still seeing occasional 429s at the very peak. Logs show fewer `rate_limited` lines.

Miguel Ramos (SRE): Good progress — that confirms the ingress was a major contributor. Next steps to harden:
- Add Redis-backed RLS to unify counters across gateway pods (recommended for multi-pod gateways).
- If you can't add RLS, increase gateway bucket-size and make sure `max-concurrent-requests` is high enough to allow short-lived spikes.
- Tune HPA metrics: use request concurrency (custom metric) instead of CPU alone.

Example minimal Redis-backed RLS values: `steady_rate=1000/min`, `burst=800` — adjust to your provisioned throughput. For testing you can deploy RLS as a small service in the same VPC.

Lee Tan (Infra): Also validate your k8s Service `externalTrafficPolicy` — if it's `Cluster`, source IPs are NATed; if you rely on per-client IP ratelimiting you may want `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. That affects how nginx and gateway see client IPs and whether ratelimiting buckets are per-IP or per-entry.

John Carver (Customer): quick note — we had externalTrafficPolicy=Cluster. Switching to Local might reduce effective worker distribution; we need to evaluate with our cloud LB. We'll test in a canary namespace.

Priya Patel (Support): We're going to open a private escalation with SRE and infra. Miguel/Lee, can you join a quick call? John, please DM your contact number and we'll set up a 15m. In the meantime, the temporary mitigation we recommend: keep ingress-limit annotations disabled, scale ingress + gateway replicas during peak windows, and add short client-side retry jitter. We'll follow up with a write-up that includes the Envoy/Redis RLS manifests and a sample kube patch for gateway flags. :white_check_mark:

Miguel Ramos (SRE): I'll prepare a minimal RLS/redis manifest and a gateway helm value diff to increase bucket/refill safely. Posting the RLS snippet here in the thread for immediate reference:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Deployment
metadata: { name: ratelimit-service }
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: ratelimit
        image: envoyproxy/ratelimit:latest
        env:
          - name: REDIS_URL
            value: redis://redis-service:6379/0
```
We'll share full manifests after the call.

John Carver (Customer): Thanks all — rolling with the ingress change plus +2 gateway replicas for the afternoon. Will send the pod logs and capture the `kubectl top` output if anything spikes. Appreciate the quick triage.

Priya Patel (Support): Thanks @John — marking this thread for escalation tasks: 1) temporary ingress annotation removal (done), 2) scale ingress+gateway (in-flight), 3) collect metrics/logs and evaluate RLS (next), 4) SRE infra call scheduled. Closing the public thread once we move to private call. :lock:
